extracted.intended_audience: NIH study-section reviewers, program officers, and researchers writing/reading molecular parasitology grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting and documenting an NIH-style research proposal (Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Vertebrate Animal section, Leadership Plan) for a molecular biology project (ribosome profiling in Trypanosoma brucei).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — clear hypothesis and enumerated aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State a central hypothesis and list discrete, testable specific aims (e.g., Aim 1: Establish the ribosome protection assay in T. brucei; Aim 2: Identify genes regulated at the level of translation during T. brucei development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise opening that frames the problem, states the hypothesis (translational controls tune protein levels within and across stages), and explains how each aim tests that hypothesis and yields deliverables/impact (new tool, identification of translated short ORFs, potential drug/vaccine targets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the study matters: disease burden (e.g., T. brucei causes sleeping sickness), gaps in knowledge (poor correlation between mRNA and protein levels; poorly understood translational control), and how the project advances the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide epidemiological context, describe current limitations (e.g., proteomics/microarrays lack resolution for low-abundance molecules), and state expected contributions (insights into translational control, improved genome annotation, relevance to drug target discovery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate novelty: adapting ribosome-profiling (NGS + ribosome footprints) to T. brucei to globally assess translational control, detect small CDSs/upstream ORFs and non-canonical initiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight technical or conceptual advances relative to prior work and how expertise of investigators enables this adaptation; indicate anticipated novel findings and future directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach — adapt and validate ribosome profiling protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed experimental plan to adapt ribosome-profiling to the organism (protocol steps: arrest translation, lyse cells, RNase digestion, density-gradient fractionation, RNA purification, library construction, NGS, informatics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include source protocols (Ingolia et al.), expected optimizations, and how each step will be implemented and validated in the chosen strain/stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish assay in standardized material (use of procyclic log-phase cultures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin assay optimization using readily available, standardized cultured log-phase procyclic forms (one liter provides sufficient material for multiple analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized conditions to optimize footprinting, library construction, and informatics before applying to more limited/complex samples (bloodstream stages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of translation arrest (cycloheximide) and rapid processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat parasites with cycloheximide in culture medium to arrest translation while maintaining ribosome positioning; rapid processing is essential to prevent changes in ribosome loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and process cells quickly (filtration, polysome buffer, flash-freeze, grind under liquid nitrogen) to preserve in vivo ribosome positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of nuclease (RNase I) and optimization of digestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use RNase I (low sequence specificity) to digest unprotected RNA and preserve ribosome-protected ~28 nt footprints; optimize conditions so unprotected RNA is fully degraded while ribosome-protected fragments are retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess digestion conditions by RNase protection assay using an in vitro-transcribed [32P]-labeled T. brucei β-tubulin fragment to choose best cleavage parameters and maintain yield of footprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate three complementary RNA preparations
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce (1) randomly-cleaved total mRNA (alkaline-cleaved), (2) randomly-cleaved mRNA associated with ribosomes (undigested ribosomal fraction), and (3) 28-nt ribosome-protected fragments (RNase-digested monosome fraction) for library construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use all three preparations for comparative RNA-seq to assess ribosome occupancy and translational efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: RNA-seq library construction to minimize sequence bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the single-stranded (ss) DNA ligase method for library construction of 28-nt fragments, which avoids sequence bias characteristic of RNA ligases (polyadenylation, oligo-dT primer containing dSpacer, CircLigase circularization, APE1 linearization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform amplification on samples with maximized full-length product but retaining unincorporated primers; compare to alternative methods to evaluate bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative SL-seq method for trypanosomatid mRNAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit the common 5' 39-nt spliced leader (SL) on trypanosomatid mRNAs to prepare SL-based libraries from intact total and ribosome-associated mRNA (first strand primed with random hexamers; second strand with SL primer) when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare SL-seq to ssDNA-ligase method for relative mRNA abundance; if comparable, prefer SL-seq for Aim 2 because it requires less input, is less costly and less labor-intensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address contamination with rRNA and small RNAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate ribosome-footprint libraries will be contaminated with rRNA (~80% in yeast) and small RNAs (siRNAs); evaluate over-representation of repeat-derived small RNAs and remove contaminants computationally or experimentally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: computational removal; rRNA capture with complementary biotinylated oligonucleotides; duplex-specific nuclease depletion (Illumina); differential salt-extraction to remove siRNAs; note that SL-seq minimizes contamination but cannot be used for footprint samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing platform and bioinformatics pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence libraries on Illumina Genome Analyzer IIx; enter fastq files into an RNA-seq pipeline (e.g., Bowtie alignment) and use scripts to quantitate reads per mRNA, aided by mapped 5' and 3' ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage existing pipelines and experienced programmers; develop new scripts/pipelines as needed guided by published approaches (Ingolia et al.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare read densities to determine translational efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare read density between randomly-cleaved total mRNA and ribosome-associated or footprinted libraries to identify transcripts preferentially recruited to or excluded from ribosomes and to compute translational efficiency per mRNA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform gene-by-gene comparisons across stages to identify stage-regulated translation and relate changes in translation efficiency to changes (or not) in mRNA abundance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess ribosome distribution along mRNA to map coding regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use footprint read distribution to determine exact ribosome positions (codon-level resolution), identify translated ORFs, eliminate non-coding ORFs, and discover novel or non-canonical initiation codons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that protected fragments may begin upstream of the start codon (yeast: 12–13 nt upstream); evaluate mapping ambiguity due to SL proximity to initiation codon and note that only ~5–8% of T. brucei genes have SL acceptor sites <10 nt from start codon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicates and experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: Use biological and technical replicates: for each developmental stage use three biological replicates and two technical replicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ optimized protocols from Aim 1 for bloodstream-stage analyses; include internal controls and, if parasite numbers are low, pool animals or use in vitro-derived cultures as backups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include internal controls by examining transcripts/proteins already identified as subject to stage-specific translational control and confirm selected findings (e.g., synthesis of 2–3 proteins) where feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior knowledge to validate ribosome profiling results; recognize that ribosome occupation measures are one step removed from direct protein synthesis and turnover, so orthogonal confirmation is valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Make NGS sequence data available by submission to NCBI Sequence Read Archive and to specialized resources (TriTrypDB) along with processed results (read-density summaries); annotate genes showing translational regulation in GeneDB/TriTrypDB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan data sharing and integration with community databases; leverage consortium membership to facilitate deposition and annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for computational challenges and pipeline development
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate need for new scripts/pipelines to analyze footprint data (e.g., mapping footprints, identifying ORFs, comparing densities), guided by established methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe in-house bioinformatics expertise and resources (Bioinformatics Core, experienced programmers) and commitment to adapt/develop necessary tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory biosafety and hazard mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge hazards of working with vertebrate-pathogen (T. brucei 927) and state that universal precautions are observed; staff receive BSL2 and EHS training; monthly safety notes are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe training, in-lab experienced supervision, and specific biosafety practices to reduce risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals — description and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe animals to be used (rats for bloodstream form isolation: ~30 rats over two years; mice as backup: ~5 per year), routes of infection, monitoring, and terminal harvest by surgery; justify animal use versus alternatives (in vitro culture is costly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numbers, strain/vendor, pathogen-free status, expected yields, and contingency plans (pooling, in vitro cultures, monomorphic strain backup) to justify animal use scientifically and ethically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterinary care, housing, and institutional assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: State that animals are housed in a facility with PHS Assurance and USDA Research Registration, with controlled environment, attending veterinarian time, husbandry, daily checks, and protocols for euthanasia and illness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details of facility oversight, on-call backup, routine husbandry, and criteria for euthanasia if animals appear ill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions to minimize stress, discomfort and injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe monitoring frequency, veterinarian/animal staff intervention, anesthetic use (ketamine/xylazine) prior to injections and terminal surgery, and monitoring parasitemia beginning on day 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain daily monitoring, criteria for intervention/euthanasia, and steps to minimize suffering during experimental procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia methods consistent with guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: State euthanasia methods (mice by CO2 asphyxiation consistent with AVMA recommendations; terminal surgery under ketamine/xylazine with aorta cut and diaphragm cut to ensure death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AVMA and institutional guidelines; fully describe terminal procedures used to harvest parasites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PI leadership and conflict-resolution plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Define PI roles (contact PI, expertise areas) and describe conflict-resolution principles: decisions based on what will generate the most complete and quality data; joint supervision and regular (monthly) joint lab meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify division of responsibilities (scientific/administrative oversight, direct supervision of personnel), frequency of joint meetings, and decision rule prioritizing data quality when disagreements arise.
